function.name: record_verdict
function.description: File what the owner says about the alert they are answering. Use this whenever the owner judges an alert - confirms it, denies it, corrects it, or says it was expected. A denial or a correction is filed here; it is NOT a reason to pause.

verdict.description: true_alert: real and worth the alert. false_alarm: nothing and nobody was there. real_but_wrong: real, but the alert described it wrongly or missed part of it. expected: real but expected - the owner themself, family, a guest, a delivery, a pet. missed_event: something happened and no alert came.

note.description: One short English sentence with any detail the owner gave, or an empty string.

function.name: pause_alerts
function.description: Stop sending alerts for a while. Use ONLY when the owner, in their latest message, asks for alerts to stop, pause, or be quiet. Pausing leaves the house unwatched, so never pause for a false alarm, a correction, or a complaint - those are a verdict, not a pause.

owner_words.description: The owner's own words that ask for the pause, copied exactly from their latest message.

until.description: A 24-hour local clock time "HH:MM" if the owner named a time to pause until, otherwise omit.

minutes.description: A duration in minutes if the owner named one, otherwise omit.

camera.description: A camera name to pause only that one camera, otherwise omit to pause all cameras.

function.name: resume_alerts
function.description: Turn alerts back on for every camera. Use when the owner asks for alerts to continue or come back on.

function.name: find_alerts
function.description: Search the alerts the box has saved and get them back as JSON, most relevant first. Use when the owner asks what happened, or asks for a video or a picture. The search is by meaning, not keywords: put the owner's own description of what they want into "what" (for example "delivery", "someone at the gate", "a dog"), and add the time they named. Then read the returned summaries and answer from them. With no arguments it returns the most recent day.

time_from.description: Start of a time range, 24-hour local "HH:MM".

time_to.description: End of a time range, 24-hour local "HH:MM".

last_hours.description: Look back this many hours, for "the last N hours".

latest.description: true for "the last alert" or "the latest".

camera.description: A camera name to search only that camera.

what.description: A few words in English describing what the owner is looking for. This drives the semantic search, so paraphrase their intent ("a parcel being dropped off" rather than only "delivery").

want.description: "video" if the owner wants the footage, otherwise "text".

function.name: summarize_activity
function.description: Get everything the box saved over a period, so you can summarize it for the owner. Use this when they ask what happened, or for a summary, or 'anything today?' - NOT when they want one specific clip (use find_alerts for that). Returns the total count, a per-camera breakdown, and every saved event in time order with its one-line description and any verdict the owner already gave. Then write a short, natural summary from it - how many events, roughly when, which cameras, the notable ones - never a raw list of every line.

day.description: "today", "yesterday", or an exact date "YYYY-MM-DD". Defaults to the last day.

last_hours.description: Summarize the last this-many hours instead of a whole day.

camera.description: Limit the summary to one camera.

function.name: check_camera
function.description: Take a LIVE look at one camera right now and get a description of what is currently visible. Use this when the owner asks what is happening at this moment ('what's at the front door now?', 'check the back yard', 'is anyone outside?') - find_alerts and summarize_activity only cover what was already saved, so they cannot answer about the present. A live photo is sent to the owner with your reply.

camera.description: The name of the camera to look at right now (one of the configured cameras).

function.name: send_clip
function.description: Attach the video of one saved alert to your reply. alert_id must be an id that find_alerts returned earlier in this same conversation. Call find_alerts first if you do not have one.

alert_id.description: The id of the alert whose video to send, from a find_alerts result.
